model: Regulated utility dividend discount at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Adjusted EPS: 3-year CAGR 6.2% (FY2022 $5.27 to FY2025 $6.31) and management's reaffirmed 5-7% long-term target through 2030. Not the equity CAGR -- see the divergence warning.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (0.7% 3-year, 1.5% 5-year, total equity including NCI and preferred) diverges far more than 30% from EPS and revenue growth. Book equity was held back by the 2022-2023 Commercial Renewables impairments and exit and by a 65-75% payout; it understates earnings power, so it is not used as the growth anchor. Since FY2025 it has stepped up ($53.0bn to $57.5bn in nine months) on the Brookfield investment and retained earnings.
historical_growth.notes: eps_3yr_cagr is on ADJUSTED EPS. eps_5yr_cagr is on GAAP EPS from FY2020 $1.72, a year depressed by the Atlantic Coast Pipeline write-off, and is not meaningful. FCF CAGRs are null: reported FCF is negative at both ends of both windows (FY2020 -$1,051M, FY2022 -$5,440M, FY2025 -$1,694M), which for a utility reflects rate-base investment, not distress. SBC is about 0.3% of revenue and flat ($100M FY2022, $102M FY2025), so the SBC-adjusted series tells the same story. Dividend per share has grown only about 2% a year ($4.22 declared in FY2025, $4.34 annualised now) against about 6% EPS growth, so the payout ratio has been falling toward the bottom of the 60-70% target.

scenario_narratives.base: Duke delivers what it has guided: adjusted EPS grows 6% in 2027 and 6.5% a year through 2030 (the upper half of the 5-7% range, as management expects once the 7.8 GW of signed data-center load starts taking power from late 2027), on a $95-105bn five-year capital plan earning allowed returns near 10%. Rate cases in the Carolinas and Florida settle roughly as recent ones have. Dividend growth stays near 2% for a few years, so payout slides to 60% -- the bottom of the 60-70% target -- which is how the plan is funded alongside the Brookfield and Tennessee proceeds, the ATM forwards and the 2029 equity units. After 2030 EPS growth fades toward 3.5% and payout recovers to 65%. Terminal growth 3% is what a 65% payout and a roughly 8.6% return on retained equity sustain without new shares.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 15.4 GW late-stage large-load pipeline converts to signed contracts through 2027 and the load arrives on schedule, pushing companywide load growth to the top of 3-4% and the capital plan toward $220bn over ten years. Multi-year rate plans and performance-based ratemaking in North Carolina, South Carolina and Ohio cut regulatory lag, so earned returns sit close to allowed returns; the Carolinas utility combination delivers its efficiencies. EPS grows 7% through 2030 and fades slowly to 4%; the franchise sustains 3.5% thereafter. This needs both the demand and the regulation to cooperate, and long-term rates not to rise further.
scenario_narratives.bear: Hyperscale customers delay or downsize, so the pipeline does not convert and part of the generation build is deferred; at the same time one or more commissions push back on customer bills -- lower allowed ROEs or disallowances in the North Carolina rate cases, slower recovery of storm, coal-ash or tariff-inflated construction costs -- while refinancing $92bn of debt at 5%-plus Treasury yields eats into holding-company earnings and more equity is needed to hold the Baa2/BBB+ rating. Adjusted EPS grows only 4% a year, below the guided range, and fades to 2.5%. The dividend is protected and keeps growing about 2%, so payout rises to 68%. No dividend cut is assumed: Duke has paid for 99 consecutive years and this is a returns-compression case, not a solvency one.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A regulated utility is worth the dividends it can pay out of allowed-return earnings on a growing rate base, discounted at what equity investors require. Duke's growth is real and unusually visible, but it is capped by regulators and bought with retained earnings and new capital, so the model values the dividend stream and lets earnings growth, not free cash flow, drive it. With the ten-year Treasury above 5%, a cost of equity of 8.25% puts fair value below the market price: the market is paying about 19 times earnings and a 3.4% dividend yield, which only works out if investors accept a return of roughly 7%, less than 2 points over Treasuries, and a terminal dividend multiple above the model's 22x cap. The 15% hurdle entry price will sit far below any plausible trading range -- a utility growing 5-7% with a 3-4% yield cannot deliver 15% without a collapse in its price first, and that is a statement about the hurdle, not about Duke.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount-rate sensitivity dominates: the terminal value is most of the result, and each half point on the cost of equity moves value by roughly 10%. The 22x terminal dividend cap binds below about 7.5%, so even at a 6.25% cost of equity the base case reaches only about 127; the current price needs both a rate near 7% and an uncapped terminal multiple of about 26x dividends.
The terminal dividend multiple (about 20x, a 12-13x forward P/E) is below where US utilities have usually traded; the model assumes no return to the low-rate-era multiple.

Per-share growth already nets out planned equity issuance. If the capital plan grows faster than internally generated funds and asset sales can cover, dilution beyond the ATM forwards and 2029 equity units would cut per-share growth below the guided range.
Regulatory outcomes in North Carolina, South Carolina and Florida, and conversion of the 15.4 GW large-load pipeline, decide which scenario plays out.
Long-tail liabilities -- $9.3bn of asset retirement obligations for coal ash and nuclear decommissioning -- are assumed recoverable in rates, as they have been so far.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 112.40-134.49
data_sources.financials: DUK_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL); Q3-2026 10-Q for balance sheet, share count, nine-month adjusted EPS and dividends, equity units and ATM forwards; FY2023-FY2025 10-Ks for the adjusted EPS reconciliations and SBC
data_sources.qualitative: DUK_Analysis.json (2026-11-15): FY2026 guidance, 5-7% long-term EPS growth target, capital plan, load pipeline, rate-case and financing risks

inputs.sbc_source: Not deducted separately: the modelled stream is adjusted earnings to common, which is already after stock-based compensation expense ($95M expensed + $7M capitalised in FY2025, 10-K FY2025 lines 22699-22700; $102M cash-flow add-back). Deducting it again would double-count.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-09-30 (780M weighted basic = diluted, Q3-2026 10-Q; 779.7M outstanding at 2026-10-31 cover page)
inputs.share_count_basis: 780M, basic and diluted identical in the Q3-2026 10-Q EPS note. Held FLAT. Known non-SBC issuance exists (about 10.8M shares under ATM equity forwards settling by end-2027; $2bn of equity units converting on 2029-08-01, roughly 15-17M shares at the collar) -- about 3.4% in total. It is NOT modelled in the share count because the growth path is management's PER-SHARE adjusted EPS trajectory, which is already net of that dilution; compounding the count as well would charge it twice.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is post-interest dividends. Built in USD: 10-year US Treasury 5.15% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-11-13) + beta 0.6 x 5.0% equity risk premium = 8.15%, rounded up to 8.25%. Same rate in all three scenarios -- risk is carried in the flows and the weights, not in the rate. Cross-check: state commissions currently allow Duke 9.6-11.0% ROE, which is the regulators' (generous) estimate of the same number; Duke's own goodwill-test WACC was 6.5-6.8% at August 2025.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable on this route: lease cost and lease interest are inside net income, and no debt of any kind is deducted in the bridge. Lease liabilities about $1.8bn at FY2025.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows: adjusted earnings are attributable to Duke Energy common stockholders, after the Brookfield minority share of Florida Progress (NCI $2,165M at 2026-09-30, rising toward a 19.7% stake) and after Series A preferred dividends ($973M preferred). Nothing further is deducted in the bridge.
inputs.bvps_memo: Common book value per share $69.75 at 2026-09-30 ((55,377 stockholders' equity - 973 preferred) / 780M). FY2026E adjusted ROE on that book about 9.7%.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE. Duke Energy is a rate-regulated electric and gas utility holdco. The dcf-methods routing table has no utility row, so this was routed on its stated principle -- discount the flow the business actually produces, at the rate appropriate to whom it accrues. An owner-FCF DCF does not work here: reported FCF has been negative in 15 of the last 18 years (FY2025 -$1,694M; OCF $12,330M against capex $14,024M) because a utility's capex is rate-base growth that regulators allow it to earn on, funded with new debt and equity rather than from operating cash flow. Discounting those negative interim flows and then subtracting $92bn of debt gives the meaningless answer Auckland Airport's first build gave. What an owner actually receives is the dividend, and what grows it is allowed-ROE earnings on a growing rate base. So: a three-scenario dividend discount model at the cost of equity, run through the Drivers engine with net debt held at ZERO (the flow is after interest; total debt $92,789M and cash $451M are recorded for reference only and must not be subtracted). ENGINE MAPPING: 'revenue' = adjusted earnings available to common ($M); 'ebitda_margin_path' = dividend payout ratio (%); SBC, D&A, capex, tax and working-capital drivers are all zero because every one of those is already inside net income; 'wacc' = cost of equity; 'terminal_cap_multiple' is a cap on the terminal price-to-dividend multiple (22x = a 4.5% dividend-yield floor). So 'adj_ebitda' and 'fcf' in the projections are DIVIDENDS, and every EBITDA or FCF multiple in the generated file is really a dividend multiple. ANCHORS. base_revenue 5,265 = FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance midpoint $6.75 ($6.70-$6.80, narrowed 2026-11-05) x 780M shares; nine-month actual adjusted EPS is $5.35 against $4.81, so the midpoint needs a $1.40 fourth quarter against $1.50 a year earlier and is not a stretch. FY0 is FY2026E, six weeks from complete, so year 1 is FY2027; this ignores the final 2026 quarterly dividend and is slightly conservative. last_fcf 3,385 = annualised dividend $4.34 ($1.085 quarterly) x 780M; reported_fcf is set equal to it so the owner-FCF identity holds on this route -- the GAAP free cash flow figure is the -$1,694M above. Adjusted EPS history: $5.27 (2022), $5.56 (2023), $5.90 (2024), $6.31 (2025), $6.75 (2026E). HOUSE/STREET BAND: collapsed -- SBC is inside the earnings stream on both bases, so there is no separate street value. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print.

bear.narrative: EPS growth falls below the guided range to 4% and fades to 2.5%; the dividend keeps growing about 2% a year so payout drifts up to 68%.

base.narrative: Growth is adjusted-EPS growth; margin is dividend payout. EPS at the middle of 5-7% in 2027, upper half 2028-2030 as guided, fading to 3.5%. Payout drifts to 60% while the capital plan peaks, then recovers to 65%.

bull.narrative: Top of the 5-7% range through 2030 and a slower fade as the large-load pipeline converts; terminal growth 3.5%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 22x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25%, above the 15% house default: earnings depend on seven state commissions plus FERC, the balance sheet needs continuous market access, and a 5%-plus ten-year Treasury is a live headwind for a bond-proxy with $92bn of debt. Base 50%: it is management's own guided range, and Duke has delivered about 6% adjusted EPS growth for three years. Bull 25%, below the 35% default: it needs a still-uncontracted data-center pipeline to convert AND constructive rate outcomes in several states at once.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
